Luxembourg–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg–Germany Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1958, as amended by Protocols of 1993 and 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (Luxembourg AML/CFT law); Règlement CSSF N° 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012, version consolidée (AML/CFT obligations for financial and non-financial professionals); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Luxembourg UBO register law), as amended and subject to restricted-access interpretation following CJEU joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (22 November 2022); pertinent EU AML Directives transposed into national law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / official extract for each foreign corporate partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of formation (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, commercial registries)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is party to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise full consular legalization through the competent Luxembourg embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or equivalent estoppel certificate for each foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or competent tax authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as above, followed by certified French or German translation if required by the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identity and address evidence for each ultimate beneficial owner (passport or national ID and proof of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the notary seal is foreign; alternatively, attestation before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft/executed notarial deed of the SCSp (acte constitutif / statuts coordonnés)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed before a Luxembourg notary; internal Luxembourg legalization only, no apostille or consular process required within Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, gérants, authorised signatories, and shareholders with >25% economic interest against: the Luxembourg CSSF AML/CFT caution lists; the UN Consolidated List; the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; OFAC SDN and associated lists; the Luxembourg FIU (CRF) advisories; and FATF public statements. PEPs and family/close associates are identified at onboarding under FATF recommendations; enhanced due diligence is triggered for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and unusual aviation/catering payment flows. Sanctions hits, unexplained wealth, or false beneficial-ownership declarations automatically preclude incorporation until fully cleared by the Luxembourg AML compliance officer and legal counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / e-RCS portal (https://www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All constitutional documents submitted to the RCS must be in French or accompanied by a certified French translation. Company names may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another Latin-script language; non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters in the deed. The corporate name of a Société en Commandite Spéciale must include 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp', and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit / Caisse (requires CSSF prior authorization)
Fonds / SICAV / SICAF / OPC / Investissement (requires CSSF authorization or specific regulated status)
Université / École (requires education ministry authorization or charter)
État / National / Grand-Ducal (requires Ministry of Justice authorization for use in a corporate style)
Luxembourg / Grand-Duché (subject to availability and official-competence review by LBR)
Red Cross / Croix-Rouge / Olympic / IO-identifying emblems (protected by statutory recognition and cannot be adopted as company tokens)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name by the LBR/RCS, the applicant may request written grounds and file a re-consideration request within 15 calendar days. If the refusal is maintained, a formal appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal administratif (Luxembourg administrative court) within one month of notification, with the refusal letter annexed and legal argument on confusion, public order, or protected tokens. A name reservation may be extended for an additional 30 days by payment of the applicable LBR extension fee before the initial window expires; failure to extend releases the name back to general availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may satisfy the formal registered-office/registered-agent requirement for the SCSp if a Luxembourg licensed domiciliation company (approved under the Law of 31 May 1999 relating to domiciliation companies) maintains the registered address and corporate records. A virtual office is not acceptable for the airline in-flight catering activity itself; the undertaking must hold a real production and ramp-delivery facility at Luxembourg Airport or an approved bonded catering kitchen subject to food-safety and customs licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 80–90% probability within the first 12 months of licensed operation due to mandatory food-safety inspections under Luxembourg food law, airport security/aviation audits, customs surveillance of bonded catering zones, and labour inspections for kitchen staff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff scale for partnerships; no minimum capital charge, approximate market range USD 2,000–3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration under the RBE register (bénéficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR filing fee for the beneficial-owner declaration; mandatory statutory filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and RCS conflict search / non-confusion certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free public database search; the Luxembourg notary may absorb the verification in the notarial fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization and certified translation bundle for foreign corporate documents (corporate shareholders' extracts, certificates of good standing, UBO IDs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign registries/foreign ministries, plus Luxembourg certified translator and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille/consular fees plus prevailing Luxembourg translator/notary translation tariff (approximately USD 300 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg corporate/M&A legal due-diligence memo and SCSp partnership agreement drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (Avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for pre-incorporation, AML/UBO, and partnership structuring at USD 300–450/hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-application dossier for aviation inflight catering/food-safety license and airport ramp access (fee and professional administrative workup)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Health / Administration des Services Vétérinaires (ASV) in coordination with Luxembourg Airport operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ministerial/administrative fee schedules plus consulting fee for preparation of premises, HACCP and customs-bonded documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, and Law of 12 July 2013 on the Société en Commandite Spéciale (sections 101-122 relating to partnerships; Article 14 for SCSp non-legal personality and pass-through tax election)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the RCS online platform (rbe.lu for beneficial ownership filings)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) / Certificate of Formation (Acte de Constitution) filed with the RCS; registration excerpt (Extrait du RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for SCSp; contributions are determined contractually in the partnership agreement. No escrow account or bank certificate required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) hereby adopts the partnership agreement as filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, accepts the subscription commitments of the limited partners, and confirms the initial partners’ contributions as per the contribution schedule. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [address] in Luxembourg, and that the General Partner’s designated officers be and are hereby appointed as Managing Director and Compliance Officer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute aviation catering contracts, and file all statutory registrations including the RCS, UBO registry, and food business licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RCS Name Reservation Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a prior name reservation application through the RCS online portal (guichet.lu) including the proposed corporate name and the activity scope 'airline catering and in-flight meal production'. Obtain a negative certificate attesting that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registrations.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Copy of passport of the partner submitting the request
Power of attorney if submitted by an authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of similarity, the applicant may amend the proposed name (add distinguishing letters/numbers) and resubmit within 5 business days without additional fee; objections from existing entities may require a withdrawal or authorization letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or any Luxembourg civil-law notary/public deed; alternatively private written agreement if not forming a real-estate SCSp (consult recommended for institutional investors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement in English, French or German with a certified translation to Luxembourgish or French if required. Define the general partner (asset manager), limited partners, capital contributions, profit allocation, management powers, transfer restrictions, and dissolthent provisions. Execute by all partners. For notarized formation, the notary files the deed with the RCS; for private deed, the general partner files the agreement and a notarized signature authority if required.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed or written partnership agreement
Identity documents and proof of address for all partners (passport or ID, utility bill)
Net worth or professional qualification statement for general partner (if required by AML due diligence)
Power of attorney for any non-resident partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the partnership agreement due to missing mandatory clauses (e.g. legal form, duration, registered office), the parties may execute an addendum to the agreement correcting the deficiencies and refile; unsigned articles are cured by obtaining original signatures and resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), Section VII Partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation file on the RCS e-registration portal (rcs.lu). Pay the registration fee. The RCS issues an excerpt (Extrait du RCS) confirming the SCSp is registered; then file the statutory publication with the Luxembourg Official Gazette (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations, RESA).
required_dossiers: Previously executed partnership agreement (notarized or private deed)
Certificate of registered office authority (letter from the lessor of the registered office address)
Identification of managers and evidence of identity
Negative certificate for name
RCS registration form signed by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query (e.g. defective registered office evidence), respond within 15 days with corrected documents; if the query is unresolved, the filing fee is refunded and a new submission must be made after correcting the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for VAT / Non-resident tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial ownership declaration with the RBE within 10 days of RCS registration, listing all individuals who, directly or indirectly, hold more than 25% interest or voting rights. Obtain the RBE registration number. Simultaneously file the taxpayer identification application (form 100) with the ACD and apply for a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA) if taxable one-stop shop or direct sales.
required_dossiers: RBE beneficial ownership declaration
Documentary evidence of ownership percentages (partnership agreement, contribution schedule)
Form 100 – Luxembourg resident tax registration or non-resident tax identification
VAT registration form (form 105) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declares a mismatch with the partnership agreement, file an amendment within 10 days; if the ACD delays tax registration, the applicant may request an expedited process via eCDF (electronic tax declaration) and may rely on the RCS excerpt as temporary evidence of formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and deposit of contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial sector entity authorized in Luxembourg (bank, payment institution) regulated by CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain a Luxembourg-based bank account for the SCSp. Submit the RCS excerpt, partnership agreement, beneficial ownership declaration, and AML/KYC package. Execute the account opening agreement and fund the capital contributions as per the schedule (no minimum required). Obtain a bank reference letter confirming the account is active and the contributions are booked.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt (Certificate of registration)
RBE registration PDF (proof of UBO declaration)
Partnership agreement
AML/KYC documentation (passport of partners, proof of funds, source of wealth)
Bank account application form
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence documents (e.g. organizational chart, FATCA/CRS self-certifications), supply within 20 business days. If the account is declined due to the catering activity's aviation-bonded nature, submit a supporting letter from the Ministry of Health and an existing airline contract; if unresolved, choose an alternative bank and apply anew in expedited mode.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, in coordination with the Ministry of Health (for food safety), and the Administration de l'environnement (for environmental permitting)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement de restauration collective (Operating Authorization for Collective Catering Establishment) and Sanitary Approval under EU Regulation (EC) No 852/2004

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg) in consultation with the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report if annual production capacity exceeds 300 tonnes of cold meat products or volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions above 100 t/year; otherwise Category C – Environmental Registration / Notice of Compliance required for industrial food production installations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 September 2020 on wastewater discharge to public sewer (pH 6.5-9, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L); VOC emission limit ≤ 75 mg/Nm³ for air ventilation at the catering kitchen; hazardous waste storage labeled and removed by authorized waste carriers; European Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/456 on Best Available Techniques (BAT) conclusions for the food, drink and milk industries, where applicable

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for commercial kitchen operators; structural load inspection certificate for roof and ventilation systems from an approved bureau de contrôle (e.g. Luxcontrol, SOCOTEC Luxembourg); occupational clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering workplace ventilation, noise exposure (action level 80 dB), food-handling health clearance, and compliance with Article L.211-1 of the Labour Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for commercial registration; electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors must file the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through a Luxembourg-registered professional. The SCSp has no minimum capital requirement; a private partnership agreement is sufficient unless the contribution comprises real estate. Required filings include the partnership agreement, identity/KYC documents of all partners, registered office address proof, manager appointment details, and evidence of the registered office. After RCS registration, the SCSp obtains a Luxembourg commercial registration number and a national identification number (NIF). For VAT, the SCSp or, if applicable, the foreign non-established taxable person must file the VAT registration questionnaire (form submitted via MyGuichet) with AEDT, stating the ISIC 5621 in-flight catering activity, estimated turnover, place of economic activity, and bank details. AEDT then issues a Luxembourg VAT number with the 'LU' prefix. For food production and ramp delivery, the ALVA/health ministry approval is a prerequisite before taxable activity starts. A non-established foreign airline caterer making taxable ground supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with AEDT from the first taxable supply, with no turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: An SCSp has no separate legal personality and is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax. Profits and losses are passed through to partners, and Luxembourg-source character is preserved at partner level. Non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment are not subject to Luxembourg direct taxation on non-Luxembourg-source income. For VAT, the SCSp itself is treated as a separate taxable person when it independently carries on an economic activity; income-tax transparency does not prevent VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg domestic law does not provide a check-the-box election comparable to the US. The SCSp is statutorily transparent; there is no domestic election to convert it into a corporate income taxpayer. Foreign partners may make classification elections in their home jurisdiction (e.g., US Form 8832), but such elections do not alter Luxembourg tax qualification. Luxembourg VAT grouping under Article 60 of the VAT Law may be elected by closely related Luxembourg-established persons subject to AEDT approval. ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules apply and override divergent tax treatment of the SCSp across jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Loi du 12 février 1979 relative à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, as amended, implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for the Luxembourg small-business exemption (Art. 57 VAT Law) applicable only to Luxembourg-established taxable persons. A non-established foreign entity has no small-business threshold and must register from the first taxable supply. Airline inflight catering involving B2B supplies to carriers will in practice exceed the threshold and requires VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system, nor does it mandate government API stamping or digital fiscal stamps. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G contracts using PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format; B2B e-invoicing is permitted with recipient consent. Invoices must preserve authenticity, integrity and legibility. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through the e-CDF/MyGuichet portal. The taxpayer must retain the standard audit file (SAF-T) and supporting transaction documents for at least six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union by the supplier or a third party acting on its behalf, including supplies of in-flight meals and catering stores loaded on aircraft that leave EU airspace on international routes. The airline operator must confirm the non-EU destination and the flight schedule. Supplies to aircraft on intra-EU routes are not automatically zero-rated and may be subject to Luxembourg VAT or the destination Member State's rules; zero-rating can also apply for intra-EU dispatch of goods to a VAT-registered acquirer in another Member State where all dispatch evidence is held. The supplier must possess conclusive proof of export within the statutory time frame, including customs export documentation and transport/route evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export declaration accepted by customs)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / aircraft manifest showing the aircraft's non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/peripheral forex confirmation evidencing repatriation of export payment proceeds
Detailed VAT invoice referencing the zero-rated export supply and the airline contract
International airline catering contract designating non-EU flight routes
ALVA/aviation food safety and bonded-store certificate for the catering kitchen and ramp delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and assess VAT at the standard rate (or the applicable reduced rate for qualifying food) if export proof is incomplete, payment is not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, or the goods never leave the EU. Default interest accrues on unpaid VAT, and administrative penalties apply per Luxembourg tax law. For fraudulent export claims, forged customs documents, or artificial routing schemes, the penalty may reach up to 100% of the evaded VAT, the normal statute of limitations may be extended to 10 years, and criminal tax fraud sanctions can include imprisonment up to 5 years and substantial fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Central Bank of Luxembourg, member of the Eurosystem. No separate Foreign Exchange Administration exists; the BCL and the Ministry of Finance administer Luxembourg's external-monetary framework, while the CSSF supervises credit institutions for AML/CFT conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the EU acquis in full. The euro is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions, including cross-border trade settlements, inbound partnership capital contributions, and profit allocations to non-resident partners. There are no exchange-control licensing requirements, no non-resident clearance permits, and no BCL approval for profit remittance. Profits allocated to non-resident partners are remitted without Luxembourg withholding tax where the SCSp is fiscally transparent and the partner is not a Luxembourg resident; applicable frictions are limited to CRS/FATCA reporting, UBO register obligations, and economic-substance requirements for the operational catering activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds to the BCL or any foreign-exchange authority, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to foreign-currency export receivables. The airline catering SCSp may retain export receipts in EUR, USD, or other convertible currencies, convert them at freely negotiated market rates, or use them directly to fund operational liabilities. The only statutory layer is BCL external-statistics reporting (balance-of-payments data), which must be submitted through the resident credit institution according to the BCL's periodic reporting cycle.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR/USD Treasury Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account with Commercial Letter of Credit and Trade Finance Lines
SWIFT MT103 Settlement Account and Transactional Banking Platform

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Euro Account for SEPA and Payroll

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EU/EEA-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 and CSSF Circular 21/785 vetting; LOW for offshore digital EMIs outside the EEA. An SCSp may hold low-value operational funds in an EMI client-money account, but cannot rely on EMI rails for high-volume aviation catering settlements, airport-ramp disbursements, or trade-finance documentation. Offshore digital EMIs without an EEA branch are legally unsuitable for the SCSp's treasury strategy because they are not SEPA-compliant, create BCL reporting gaps, and are generally rejected by Luxembourg credit institutions for correspondent clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law does not impose a universal physical-appearance requirement, but the CSSF's risk-based KYC guidance and common bank practice require at least one principal of the SCSp — usually the general partner's manager or a Luxembourg-regulated professional representative — to attend an initial business-intention and identity interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises. Remote onboarding is permitted only where identity verification is performed through an eIDAS-qualified electronic identification method or a notarised apostilled identity package; foreign directors acting as UBOs generally cannot satisfy tier-1 bank expectations through remote video alone.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and fiscal-transparency opacity of the SCSp, especially where the general partner is a professional service company and limited partners are non-resident holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised SCSp partnership agreement; current RCS extract; UBO declaration filed with the Luxembourg business register under the Law of 13 January 2019; an organisational chart covering every partner with a 25% or greater interest; constitutional documents of all partner entities; passport and proof of residential address for each beneficial owner; subscribed-capital schedule; and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the SCSp is fiscally transparent and engaged in a genuine commercial catering activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure through aviation clients, airline intermediaries, ramp-side counterparties, and cross-border procurement of catering inputs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening policy covering EU, UN, OFAC, and UK lists; negative screening reports for all airlines and suppliers; food-import and health-authority licences demonstrating the origin and safety of goods; complete airline counterparty due-diligence files; and a compliance memorandum confirming that catering materials are ordinary foodstuffs outside dual-use or aviation-security export-control regimes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency institutional inflows resembling money transmission or an unlicensed payment-collection business, triggering suspicion of treasury-centre or financial-audit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed inflight-catering master service agreements and applicable rate cards; invoices and delivery manifests proving physical meal delivery to aircraft at ramp positions; payroll and Luxembourg social-security filings for kitchen and ramp staff; lease agreements and airport-authority permits for the catering kitchen; and an independent tax opinion classifying the revenue as ordinary commercial income under Article 1821 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons or FATF high-risk-jurisdiction investors connected to capital escrow or profit-repatriation flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration forms; comprehensive source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports; notarised evidence of asset origin and sales proceeds; family-relationship disclosures; relevant foreign tax returns; enhanced due-diligence questionnaires; and a legal memorandum prepared by Luxembourg counsel on the ownership and control structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Investor capital must be wired from the investor's own bank account via SWIFT MT103, or via SEPA Credit Transfer when the remitter uses EUR, to the SCSp's designated capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution. Each instruction must identify the investor as originator, the SCSp as beneficiary with its unique IBAN, and a payment reference such as 'Capital Call No. [x] — Subscription Agreement dated [y]'. Where the receiving bank's schema requires an ISO 20022 purpose code, the code CAPT (capital transfer) is the standard election. The bank will verify the remitter against the investor register, screen sanctions and embargoes, request underlying subscription documents, and block any third-party payment without a documented contribution or assignment agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The SCSp will use SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) for euro-denominated payroll, domestic utilities, and low-value catering supplies; SWIFT MT103 for USD, GBP, and other non-euro trade settlements; and irrevocable confirmed commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600, issued through BIL or BGL BNP Paribas, for high-value capital procurement such as kitchen fit-out works, cooling trucks, and aircraft loading equipment. Recurring monthly airline collections may be structured through SEPA Direct Debit mandates or automated SWIFT customer credit-transfer arrangements, with a central-liquidity sweep into the main operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge monthly USD revenue streams from airline clients
FX options (European-style calls and puts) acquired on a non-leveraged basis to cover contingent currency exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/USD) entered into in connection with long-term debt financing of the catering kitchen and ramp-logistics assets
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only where a customer currency is not freely deliverable in the EEA, and the NDF is booked through a Luxembourg or EEA-licensed bank counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual accounts filing and publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, annual accounts must be approved by the partners within six months of year-end and filed with RCSL within one month of approval; standard deadline for calendar-year entities is 31 July. For non-calendar year-ends, the filing must be lodged within one month of approval and no later than seven months after the financial year-end, unless the SCSp is exempt from publication under the Law of 19 December 2002.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers administrative fines (up to EUR 5,000); repeated defaults may lead to RCSL administrative strike-off and court-ordered dissolution; the general partner and managers may be jointly liable for resultant damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs (annual beneficial-owner confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE), operated by RCSL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for all registered entities, irrespective of whether partnership interests changed; any change in ownership or beneficial ownership occurring during the year must be declared within one month and is separately subject to the annual confirmation protocol.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or non-confirmation exposes the entity and responsible persons to fines under the UBO Law (up to EUR 250,000 for entities and EUR 125,000 for individuals; up to EUR 1,250,000 in aggravated professional cases), and may result in suspension of registry filings or administrative strike-off by RCSL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt du rapport du réviseur d'entreprises (filing of statutory auditor's report when audit is mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCSL together with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be issued before the partners' annual meeting and filed with RCSL together with the approved annual accounts; for calendar-year entities the combined deadline is 31 July (one month after the six-month approval period).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registered auditor must file with the RCSL any refusal or qualification; failure to obtain the audit, when required, constitutes a criminal offence under Luxembourg company law and renders the annual accounts ineffective for publicity purposes, with fines and strike-off exposure for management.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit becomes mandatory if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three Luxembourg thresholds on the balance sheet date: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million and average workforce exceeding 50 employees; audit is also required for regulated SCSp or AIF vehicles, public-interest entities, and where the partnership agreement expressly requires an independent réviseur d'entreprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial and companies register and annual accounts), transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted for consolidated or regulated-fund reporting; the SCSp's accounts must be prepared and presented in EUR or its functional currency with Lux-GAAP-compliant notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Luxembourg-registered SCSp must maintain accurate beneficial-ownership records and confirm them electronically in the RBE every calendar year before 31 March, regardless of transfers; in addition, any transfer of partnership interests that results in a change of UBO data must be filed with the RBE within one month of the transfer. The annual confirmation covers the list of partners, ownership percentages, and identity data used for AML/KYC.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (limited partners and general partner, with ownership percentages)
Register of partnership-interest transfers and encumbrances
Minute book of partner resolutions and general-partner decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no statutory audit applies; USD 10,000 – USD 25,000 if audit thresholds are exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% of qualifying investments), participation exemption (100% exemption on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings), notional interest deduction (NID) for equity financing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 600 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via eCDF (Electronic Tax Filing System) at impotsdirects.public.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extension to 31 December available upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For SCSp, report the entity's net income as allocated to each partner; non-resident partners must attach a schedule of their share.
Non-resident partners must ensure their share of non-deductible expenses is correctly reflected; no specific non-resident filing requirement beyond the partnership return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credits on their own tax returns; the partnership return only records the credits at entity level if applicable.
SCSp is generally exempt from net wealth tax; if not, non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on their share.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, with a minimum of EUR 100; additional interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; criminal sanctions for intentional non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the recipient holds at least 10% for 12 months; treaty rates may apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from their jurisdiction and complete Form 22 (withholding tax exemption certificate) to the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD) prior to payment. The form must be filed electronically via eCDF, and the TRC must be certified within the last 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if the recipient is an EU company holding at least 25% for 2 years); Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under the same directive; treaty rates may apply).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; Master File required if group turnover exceeds EUR 100 million; both thresholds based on consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and substance requirements apply. An SCSp must demonstrate adequate substance (e.g., real office, employees, decision-making in Luxembourg) to avoid being classified as a shell company and to benefit from tax treaties and EU directives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets in the SCSp's tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 100% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years (Luxembourg Criminal Code Art. 396).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no physical presence, no employees, no real business activity, and is used solely to channel profits without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; penalties up to EUR 250,000 under GAAR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for additional taxes and penalties if they fail to ensure substance; potential criminal charges for abuse of law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct adequate customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records for the catering business's financial flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering (Luxembourg AML Law of 2004).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; travel bans may be issued during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing in transactions with related parties (e.g., catering services to airline affiliates).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 10% of the adjustment amount, and interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; potential criminal liability for tax fraud.
